title: Glossary entry
description: content/glossary/<id>.yaml: one defined term, acronym or phrase. Text links to an entry with [[id]] or [[id|shown text]]; the website and the print and ebook editions resolve every link to this record. See docs/terminology.md.

id.description: Stable identifier used in [[id]] links. Must match the file name.

term.description: The headword as it should normally be written, with its capitalization (e.g. 'Native nations', 'ADR').

kind.description: term: a word the project defines for its own usage; acronym: an abbreviation (needs 'expansion'); legal-term: a term defined by a statute, regulation or court, which must cite that source; phrase: a set expression.

expansion.description: For acronyms: the words written out, e.g. 'alternative dispute resolution'. The first link in each chapter or web page prints the expansion followed by the acronym.

usage.description: preferred: use by default; acceptable: correct but not the default; context-only: use only in the stated context (e.g. quoting a statute); avoid: do not use in the project's own voice. The text checker flags 'avoid' terms outside quotations.

definition.description: Markdown. May cite sources with [@key] and link other entries with [[id]].

usage_note.description: Markdown. When and how to use the term, and what to write instead where relevant.

aliases.description: Other spellings and forms (plurals, possessives) that the text checker treats as this term when it looks for unlinked uses.

use_instead.description: For 'avoid' and 'context-only' entries: the ids of the entries to use instead.

sources.description: Keys of content/sources records relied on for the definition or usage. A 'legal-term' entry needs at least one.

basis.description: Whether the entry restates sources, records the project's own choice, or both (charter, commitment 8).

since.description: Content version in which the entry was first published.

redirect_to.description: For a retired entry: where old [[id]] links now point. Ids are never reused.
